The apple is whole: "The apple is whole" refers to the state of an apple that has not been cut or sliced and retains its original round shape. Even if it has been peeled or cooked, it is still applicable as long as it retains its original round shape.
The apple is peeled: "The apple is peeled" refers to the state of an apple that has had its skin removed by peeling. It does not apply if the apple has been cut or cooked without being peeled. If the apple is cooked, we don't say it is peeled.
The apple is grated: "The apple is grated" refers to the state of an apple that has been shredded into fine pieces using a grater. Sometimes grating can release moisture, but 'grated' refers to the presence of coarse grains. It no longer applies to smooth smoothies or sauces made by mixers or blenders.
The apple is cut: "The apple is cut" refers to the state of an apple that has been coarsely split into 2 or 3 pieces. If is sliced into small pieces, we don't say it is cut. It doesn't matter whether the apple is peeled or not.
The apple is sliced: "The apple is sliced" refers to the state of an apple that has been cut into thin or narrow pieces. It does not include the case where the apple is split into two or three large pieces. Even if it is cooked, it is still applicable as long as it retains the shape of the pieces.
The apple is cooked: "The apple is cooked" refers to the state of an apple that has been sufficiently heated in any way.
The apple is baked: "The apple is baked" refers to the state of an apple that has been cooked in an oven.
The apple is smooth: "The apple is smooth" refers to the state of an apple that has been squeezed or blended into a smooth texture. If the apple has turned to a liquid(completely juiced), we don't say it is smooth.
The apple is dried: "The apple is dried" refers to the state of an apple that has been dried by removing moisture. This can be done by various methods, such as drying in the sun, drying in the oven, or drying in a dehydrator.
The apple is mixed with other ingredient: "The apple is mixed with other ingredients" refers to the state of apple combined with other components in a recipe. It is applicable only when we can see multiple ingredients are mixed. If they have dissolved into a single object, the state doesn't apply. It doesn't refer to adding only seasonings or water. This state is not affected by the fact it is cooked or not.
The apple is caramelized: "The apple is caramelized" refers to the state of apple that has been cooked with brown sugar, typically until it turns a golden brown color.
